transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we know, I've been keeping Grandma's collection of 42 coins since she passed, and with my move to a smaller apartment coming up, we need to settle what happens to the collection. Before I put together a plan, I'd like to do our usual family check-in. Jordan and Rosa, is there anything you think I should know that might shape how I approach this? Anything at all -- now's the time to mention it.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should mention that last month I got a written assessment from our family appraiser, Helen Park. She said the three 1909 Lincoln cents in the collection need to stay together and should be stored in acid-free capsules. I don't think her assessment has reached the rest of the family yet, so I wanted to put that on the table before you make the plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have something to share too. I have a dated birthday card from Grandma where she promised me the 1921 Morgan silver dollar from the collection. I haven't shown it to either of you yet, but I wanted to put it on the table now, before you make the plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for putting these items on the table. I want to get this right before I make my final decision.
